Type 1 Zoning Map Amendment
Substitute Narrative, Analysis and Plans
223 West Erie Street
DX-5 District to DX-5 District (Type 1)

223 W Erie Conversion LLC is the “Applicant” for a Type 1 Zoning Map Amendment for the subject property
located at 223 West Erie Street from the DX-5 Downtown Mixed-Use District to the DX-5 Downtown Mixed-
Use District (Type 1) to redevelop the existing 7-story building and allow a change of use from ground floor
retail/commercial and office use above to ground floor retail/commercial and residential use above.

The site is bounded by West Erie Street to the north, commercial property to the east, an 18-foot public
alley on the south, and North Franklin Street to the west. The subject property consists of approximately
11,200 square feet of site area and is improved with an over 100-year-old commercial building which
occupies substantially all of the site. The existing building contains approximately 56,000 square feet of
floor area and was previously operated as retail/commercial space on the ground floor and office space
above. There are no off-street vehicular parking spaces on site. The property is a transit-served location
based on its proximity to the CTA Brown Line and Purple Line Express station entrance at Chicago/Franklin
and Chicago Avenue bus corridor.

The Applicant proposes to complete a historic rehabilitation of the existing building to upgrade aged and
substandard components of the structure and convert the 2nd through 7th floors to residential use. The
building will contain a total of 66 residential units (34 dwelling units and 32 efficiency units). The ground
floor will continue to be operated as retail/commercial space and the building footprint will remain
unchanged. The Applicant proposes to add 34 bicycle parking spaces within the existing building. The
Applicant is seeking all relief necessary, as allowed by the Chicago Zoning Ordinance, for the attached
plans.

adjustment to reduce the minimum required on-site open space from 1,260 square feet to zero square feet
(3) a variation to reduce the minimum required rear setback for floors containing dwelling units from 30 feet
to zero feet; and (4) a variation to reduce the required off-street loading from one space to zero spaces.
